subject: ACME POC: trial integration plan and success criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lee <sara.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: ACME POC: trial integration plan and success criteria

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for taking the time to meet this morning. Big appreciate you walking us through the primary evaluation goals for ACME's Classifier Assistant. Per our call, I wanted to summarize next steps and propose a minimal POC plan we can start this week.

Goal / success criteria (as discussed):
- Latency: median inference latency <= 350ms at 1 RPS for 1k token requests.
- Cost: per-inference cost target to be < 50% of current vendor (you mentioned current baseline; we should confirm after initial run).
- Accuracy/Quality: fall within +/- 5% of your current production model on your 5 canonical prompts (we'll use your test set).
- Stability: no more than 1% error/failure rate over 24h of realistic traffic.

Proposed 2-week POC (timeline):
1) Day 0–2: Access and onboarding
   - We provide test keys and a sandbox model in our hosted environment.
   - Share API integration guide and SDK snippets (attached).
2) Day 3–7: Integration & smoke tests
   - ACME implements SDK-based calls or direct REST routes.
   - Implement streaming for long responses and tool-calling hooks (we outlined suggested endpoints below).
3) Day 8–12: Evaluation run
   - Run your eval suite (5 canonical prompts + 200 random samples).
   - Collect latency/cost/quality metrics; Redwood will enable KV prefix caching and batching tunables.
4) Day 13–14: Wrap-up
   - Joint review meeting, share dashboards, decide next steps.

Ownership:
- Redwood: provide sandbox keys, integration docs, quickstart SDK examples, and one integration support session (60m).
- ACME: assign an eng lead for integration work and provide the canonical prompts + test set.

Integration notes (high level):
- SDKs: use the Redwood JS or Python SDKs for quickest integration; examples attached in api-integration-guide.md.
- REST routes: POST /v1/generate for completions; POST /v1/chat for chat-style flows; POST /v1/embeddings for similarity.
- Streaming: we support chunked server-sent events (SSE) and WebSocket streaming — recommend SSE for web clients and WebSocket for persistent connections.
- Tool calling / function hooks: provide a schema-driven function-calling interface; include tool metadata in the initial request (name, inputs schema), Redwood will surface structured tool-calling events in the response payload.

Attachments: redwood-poc-proposal.pdf (summary) and api-integration-guide.md (snippets).

Next steps I recommend:
1) Confirm people + eng lead for ACME by EOD tomorrow.
2) I’ll create sandbox keys and push the integration guide to the shared Drive once we have the eng owner.
3) Book a technical onboarding session (I’ve suggested Fri 11am PT — let me know if that works).

Thanks — excited to get this rolling.

Best,
Marissa
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
m: 415-555-0123

Tom — great to meet you (virtually). Thanks for taking point. Quick answers to your questions and a bit more detail on the integration surface: 

1) Sandbox key scoping / rate limits
- Yes — we can issue a sandbox API key scoped to a single model variant and enforce 5 RPS soft limits plus a hard quota for daily tokens. We’ll create the key once you confirm the eng lead email (we have Tom).

2) Token-level cost in dashboard
- We surface token-level breakdowns per-request and aggregate cost estimates in the Redwood Console. During the POC we’ll enable 24h retention of cost metrics for your account and share a read-only dashboard link.

3) Recommended integration pattern (minimal effort):
- If you use Redwood SDK (js/python): call client.chat.create({ model: 'rwd-llama-7b-opt', input: prompt, functions: [/* tool schema */] })
- For direct REST: POST /v1/chat with body {"model":"rwd-llama-7b-opt","messages":[...],"functions": [...] }
- Streaming: include "stream": true in the request. For SSE we push chunked events with a final "event: done" marker.
- Tool calling: we implement the OpenAI-style function-calling pattern — the response may include a "function_call" object. If present, your infra should call the named tool and then send back the result via a follow-up chat message with role "tool".

4) SDK snippets and routes (attached)
- See api-integration-guide.md for copy-paste examples and a small Node.js express sample that shows streaming + function-calling glue.

5) Support and escalation
- Rishi (cc) will be your primary CS escalation for infra/limits during the POC. He can help tune batching/caching and monitor throughput.

Proposed immediate actions:
- I’ll create the scoped sandbox key and post it to the shared Drive by 10am PT.
- Tom: can you confirm which model variant you want to test (options: rwd-llama-7b-opt, rwd-mistral-8b-q4, rwd-llama-13b-quant)? Also confirm preferred SDK (js/python).

If everything looks good I’ll book the onboarding session and include the integration sample code in the invite.

Best,
Marissa
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: api-integration-guide.md]

Thanks Marissa — that plan looks solid. A couple of technical clarifications from our eng side before we start: 

1) Streaming and partial responses: if we enable "stream": true and the model issues a function_call mid-stream, will Redwood emit the function_call event immediately (so we can call our tool) or only after the final chunk? We need mid-stream tool calls for a progressive classification UX.

2) For tool-calling, is there a recommended JSON schema validator you recommend for inputs? We run our tool gateway through Kong and would like to validate payloads client-side.

3) Are there any Terraform or IaC snippets for setting up firewall rules / IP allowlists for the sandbox endpoints? Prefer to automate key provisioning via our secrets manager.

We should be able to start integration work today once we have the scoped sandbox key.

Tom
Senior Software Engineer, ACME Corp
